messages:
elen: Anyone else seeing a big LCP spike on dashboard charts after last night's deploy? heatmaps and sparklines hang for ~400-800ms on first paint. :eyes:
aj: Yup, noticed it in canary. traces show main-thread parse + a sudden download of telemetry-client chunk. looks like the telemetry import moved into the hot path.
sophie: I rolled one user session back and the chart paint improved. canary % correlates with spike.
infra-bot: deploy "web-client@2026.03.20-telemetry-inline" finished 2026-03-20T03:12:34Z (canary 10%).
kevin: do we have a stack trace / module that caused the chunk to land in the main bundle? maybe a new top-level `import 'telemetry/client'` landed in chart widgets.
mike: grabbing bundle report now. `source-map-explorer` shows telemetry-client + intl + large geo lib grouped into same splitpoint for charts. the telemetry chunk size grew ~180KB gz -> 820KB gz.
elen: that matches. we used to lazy import telemetry in top-level app shell; yesterday's change moved `initTelemetry()` into `appBootstrap()` which now runs during widget hydration.
aj: short-term: can we lazy-init telemetry after first paint? e.g., defer in requestIdleCallback or microtask after hydration.
sophie: we hit an internal API debate: product wanted early telemetry to capture UX metrics for rollout, so they asked to initialize earlier.
kevin: tradeoff obvious. capturing early metrics vs shipping usable UX. For now can we gate early init behind canary flag? rollback would be heavier.
elen: I propose: revert change on canary (hotfix) and add a non-blocking init path:
```
// deferred telemetry
if (window.requestIdleCallback) {
  requestIdleCallback(() => import('./telemetry/client').then(m => m.init()))
} else {
  setTimeout(() => import('./telemetry/client').then(m => m.init()), 2000)
}
```
aj: also we should split telemetry-client out of chart splitpoint explicitly so charts don't pull it for hydration. That's a bundler config change (webpack/rollup splitpoint tweak).
mike: yes, we can add a manual split point: `/* webpackChunkName: "telemetry" */ import('./telemetry/client')` inside dev branch.
devex: small UX note — if we delay telemetry we might miss early click metrics for the rollout check. can we add a tiny synchronous beacon that only records immediately-visible user action (click on CTAs) and defer richer instrumentation?
sophie: agreed. a small opt-in ping would satisfy rollout criteria.
kevin: routing/quota side: I saw a storm of cache-miss-induced backend requests when charts rehydrated in parallel (canary traffic pattern). KV-prefetch affinity seems to be causing repeated misses if telemetry temp keys aren't present. could be thrashing.
elen: nice catch. sounds like two problems that amplified each other: client-side bundle moved telemetry into hot path -> parse + import delay -> many components rehydrate slowly -> router retries/prefetch misfires -> KV cache misses -> backend fanout.
aj: to mitigate quickly: 1) pause canary rollout to 0% 2) hotfix revert that moves telemetry back to idle init 3) add a temporary client-side throttle to chart rehydrations to avoid thundering requeries 4) follow-up: split telemetry chunk & add unit test for splitpoint.
mike: I can cut the hotfix PR now (revert + deferred import + small throttle). will run smoke locally and on staging.
kevin: I'll coordinate rollback of canary via deploy bot. infra-bot, please temp-scale down canary to 0.
infra-bot: rollback request acknowledged. canary scale to 0% queued. will post when complete.
sophie: once hotfix is in, let's run perf telemetry job to verify LCP back to baseline and KV-prefetch requests drop. can we add a synthetic that loads first 3 dashboards in parallel?
devex: I can add that synthetic to e2e script, will run on staging after hotfix. also putting a note in rollout doc about telemetry init decisions.
elen: thanks everyone. plan: mike hotfix PR -> kevin trigger canary pause -> run staging perf -> release rollback/hotfix to prod. we should follow up with a short RFC on telemetry vs early-init tradeoffs. :+1:
